strategy_title: Enabling TF32 + Larger Tiles Causes Register Spill Regression
strategy_description: Increasing BLOCK_M and BLOCK_N (e.g., 32→64 and 64→128) while enabling TF32 caused registers per thread to nearly double (80→156), which halved theoretical occupancy (37.5%→18.75%) and increased total executed instructions by 3.6x (5M→18M), resulting in a 1.68x longer kernel duration despite improved compute SOL (12%→26%) and reduced warp stall cycles (7.34→3.21). The root cause is that the larger tile sizes dramatically increased register pressure, preventing the compiler from keeping accumulators in registers and forcing spills, which more than offset any benefit from TF32 or better tile efficiency. When a kernel is already register-limited (Block Limit Registers was already the binding constraint at 6 blocks/SM before), enlarging tiles will worsen register pressure and cause regression even if compute utilization nominally improves.
slow_pseudocode:
BLOCK_M = 32
BLOCK_N = 64
ALLOW_TF32 = False
# registers_per_thread = 80, theoretical_occupancy = 37.5%
acc += tl.dot(a, b, allow_tf32=ALLOW_TF32)  # scalar FFMA path
fast_pseudocode:
# DO NOT DO THIS when register pressure is already the binding occupancy limiter
BLOCK_M = 64   # doubled
BLOCK_N = 128  # doubled
ALLOW_TF32 = True
# registers_per_thread = 156 (+95%), theoretical_occupancy = 18.75% (-50%)
# executed_instructions = 18.4M (+262%) -> kernel duration 88us vs 52us
applicable_when: Never applicable as described: do NOT increase tile sizes when Block Limit Registers is already the binding occupancy constraint (registers_per_thread > 64 and theoretical occupancy already limited by registers). TF32 alone (without tile size increase) may still be worth trying.
do_not_apply_when: Kernel is already register-limited (Block Limit Registers < Block Limit Warps and Block Limit Shared Mem); registers_per_thread already high (>64); grid is small (waves_per_sm < 0.5) so occupancy loss from register pressure increase cannot be compensated by more waves.
framework_notes: In Triton, BLOCK_M and BLOCK_N constexprs directly control accumulator tile size and thus register consumption. Doubling both dimensions quadruples the accumulator register footprint. ALLOW_TF32=True alone (without tile size change) should be tested separately as it does not inherently increase register pressure.

strategy_title: Adding Autotune With Empty Configs Regresses Via Register Explosion
strategy_description: Adding @triton.autotune with configs that only vary num_warps and num_stages (empty tile dicts {}) while simultaneously changing BLOCK_M from 32 to 64 caused registers per thread to jump from 94 to 254 (near hardware maximum), collapsing theoretical occupancy from 31.25% to 12.5% and achieved occupancy from 6.25% to 3.12%. Executed instructions nearly doubled (5.1M to 9.2M) and kernel duration increased by 43% (51.84us to 74.02us). The structural anti-pattern is identical to exp_001: tile sizes hardcoded as constexpr inside the kernel body are invisible to the autotuner, so the autotuner cannot select smaller tiles to relieve register pressure. The autotuner only selected a smaller block_size (128→64 threads), which halved parallelism without reducing register pressure.
slow_pseudocode:
# BEFORE: BLOCK_M=32, BLOCK_N=64, BLOCK_K=32, no autotune, 94 regs/thread
@triton.jit
def kernel(...):
    BLOCK_M: tl.constexpr = 32
    BLOCK_N: tl.constexpr = 64
    BLOCK_K: tl.constexpr = 32
    # Duration: 51.84us, Registers: 94, Executed: 5.1M inst
applicable_when: Never — this is a pure regression pattern to avoid.
do_not_apply_when: Always avoid: do not add @triton.autotune with empty Config dicts ({}) while simultaneously increasing any tile dimension (BLOCK_M, BLOCK_N, BLOCK_K). The autotuner cannot override hardcoded constexpr tile sizes inside the kernel body, so it cannot compensate for the increased register pressure. This pattern causes registers_per_thread to approach 255, theoretical occupancy to collapse, and kernel duration to increase even when block_size is reduced by the autotuner.
framework_notes: In Triton, @triton.autotune Config dicts with empty {} only control num_warps and num_stages — they do NOT affect any tl.constexpr values hardcoded inside the kernel body. To allow the autotuner to explore tile sizes, BLOCK_M/BLOCK_N/BLOCK_K must be declared as kernel parameters (not internal assignments) and included as keys in each Config dict. Setting key=[] also means no cache invalidation on shape changes.
